title: Honduras' Dengue Response in 2026: Progress and Adaptation - BORGEN
snippet: One of the clearest improvements since 2024 is the strengthening of epidemiological surveillance. During the 2024 emergency, PAHO noted that Honduras faced shortages of diagnostic kits and trained personnel, which slowed detection and complicated the classification of severe cases. In 2026, however, reporting has become more consistent and detailed. [...] For example, El Heraldo reported that by March 2026, Honduras had already identified 27 severe dengue cases out of roughly 50 confirmed infections. This level of early classification was far less common in 2024, when overwhelmed clinics struggled to differentiate between suspected, confirmed and severe cases. Faster detection allows for a quicker clinical response, more accurate resource allocation and earlier community alerts, all of which can significantly reduce mortality risk. [...] The most striking difference between the two years is the stability of early-season transmission in 2026. According to theGlobal Dengue Observatory, Honduras reported 526 dengue cases in April 2026, a figure significantly below the expected seasonal average. By mid-May, the country had registered 3,018 cases, roughly 0.4 times the expected level for that point in the year.
